subject: Post-discovery: sample corpus request for model validation
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Miller <sara@acmeinc.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Jul 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: sample corpus request for model validation

Hi Sara — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary
- You’re evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing Q&A assistant across contract and onboarding docs.
- Primary concerns: preserving PHI/PII, maintaining low-latency for short queries, and avoiding hallucinations on legal language.

What we need from ACME to make a model-fit recommendation and run a small validation: 
1) A representative sample of user queries (CSV or spreadsheet). We only need 500–2,000 rows to start — a mix of short queries and longer contextual prompts.
2) A short set (10–30) of edge-case examples that you’re most worried about (PII, contract clause references, ambiguous pronouns).
3) Any existing redaction rules you currently apply.

We created a lightweight template (attached) for the query sample — columns: query_text, source_doc_type, anonymization_required (yes/no), expected_answer_format. If you can upload the CSV or share to the Drive link below that would be ideal.

Immediate plan / timeline
- You share sample CSV + edge-case doc (this week if possible).
- We run a baseline eval against 2 candidate model variants and return: exemplar responses, latency/cost estimates, and a short redaction recommendation.
- Follow-up 30-minute review session to go over results and next steps.

Attachments: acme_user_queries_sample.csv (template), acme_edgecases_notes.docx, NDA_signed.pdf

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cDEFgh
HubSpot: HS-98765

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the template if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

--

Team — forwarding ACME’s sample export and edge-case doc (attached by the customer). High level asks from the commercial side: quick baseline by 10 Jul; guidance on minimal anonymization; recommendations on models/quant/config to balance cost/latency/accuracy.

I’m proposing the following approach for the baseline run (please confirm feasibility):
1) Candidate models to evaluate (two lanes):
   - Redwood-Open-13B-INT8: lower cost, good for short Q&A; expect faster latency with 1–2 token/static KV cache optimizations.
   - Llama2-70B-4bit: higher quality on long-context legal language but higher cost — measure cost/latency delta.

2) Eval checklist (deliverable):
   - 100 random user queries from their CSV (we can sample to avoid any PII risk).
   - 12 customer edge-case prompts run verbatim.
   - Metrics: exact-match where appropriate, F1 for extraction tasks, hallucination flag rate (manual spot-check for 30 replies), median p50/p95 latency, and tokens-per-response cost estimate.

3) Redaction guidance: propose we return a short ‘redaction rules’ doc (what to mask, suggested schema) + automated scrub script suggestion (simple regexes for emails/SSNs/phone). Marissa — can you prepare a 1-page redaction template?

Attachments (from ACME): acme_user_queries_sample.csv, acme_edgecases_notes.docx

If this plan looks good I’ll own the evaluation run; Ben I’ll need you to confirm the HubSpot link & schedule the follow-up review.

Irene
Irene Choi
Product Solutions | Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com

Hi Sara — thanks for sending the files and for the quick response. Outline of next steps and what you’ll see from us: 

What we’ll deliver by Tue, 10 Jul
- Baseline evaluation report (PDF) comparing Redwood-Open-13B-INT8 vs. Llama2-70B-4bit on your sample: 30 representative q&a examples, 12 edge-case analyses, latency and cost table, and our recommended model variant for pilot.
- One-page redaction rules doc and a small scrub script (regex-based) that your engineering/security team can run locally before sharing larger datasets.
- Short appendix with example prompts and suggested canonical prompt templates for higher-recall legal extraction.

Privacy note
- We’ll only use sampled/anonymized records for public/stored evaluation. Any raw data you prefer we keep strictly ephemeral, confirm and we’ll run locally in your VPC or on a secure ephemeral instance.

Scheduling
- I scheduled a 30-minute review for Tue, 10 Jul 2028 at 10:00 AM PT — invite should appear in your calendar. If that doesn’t work, let me know and we’ll adjust.
